body:
> Major drawback: EntityInterface would have to change since we would need to pass an SplObjectStorage to both hasErrors() and getErrors().

We'd need to have a solution that doesn't expand the method signatures. A visited set could be stored as a static attribute for the duration of the `getErrors()`/`hasErrors()` operation. There is likely also a solution that uses a 'queue' of entities to visit instead of recursion.

How about an additional property in the entity which states something like `isChecked`
Then whenever we recursivly go through all fields and sub-entities we can just skip entities which have already been checked.

I gave those solutions some thought, but there are some problems with each of them:

For any attribute (be it a static set of visited entities, or a state `isChecked` on each entity), we'd still need a way to make the *original* call to `getErrors()` or `hasErrors()` clear those attributes in the end, but the recursive calls to `getErrors()` or `hasErrors()` must not clear those attributes. And we need to most definitely clear those attributes, or subsequent calls to `getErrors()` or `hasErrors()` might return stale information.

The other solution would be to give the responsibility of recursing through the entities to the original call of `hasErrors()` or `getErrors()`. The entity could visit all entities and call `getErrors(false)` or `hasErrors(false)` on them. This however has the drawback of modifying the behavior of those methods. For example: Someone might have inherited form the Entity class to overwrite the getErrors method to restrict which associated entities it recurses into. Since the root entity would traverse all entities by itself, this implementation might break stuff.

I don't have any better solution. So we can either expand the method signatures while keeping the behaviour mostly the same, or we can alter the behaviour while keeping the method signature the same.

Okay, nevermind my previous answer. I took another look at #16588 and that solution should work. I didn't think to do it that way. I'll write a fix and some tests next week, and will also check if that fixes #16707 too.

While this would work, it would have the drawback of modifying the behavior quite significantly. As I wrote in my previous comments:

> This however has the drawback of modifying the behavior of those methods. For example: Someone might have inherited form the Entity class to overwrite the getErrors method to restrict which associated entities it recurses into. Since the root entity would traverse all entities by itself, this implementation might break stuff.

Are there any benefits I am missing?

Your first solution, as I said, does not call `getErrors` on the linked entities, which breaks the behavior if someone happened to overwrite that method in their entity classes.

Your second solution would require expanding the method's signature, which @markstory explicitly said should be avoided.

In my opinion, the solution in #16588 would be the simplest and cleanest approach. I'll write an implementation and some tests today and send over a merge request, than you can check it out and propose changes if necessary.

issue.title: Issue #17318: Cyclic Recursion while using EntityTrait::getErrors and ::hasErrors

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
See Issue #17318

To prevent infinite recursion when checking for errors in linked entities (i.e. when there are cyclic references), the methods `getErrors` and `hasErrors` now keep track of being visited in the private property `_hasBeenVisited`, which they set to `true` before recursing into entities linked to them, and set to `false` again afterwards. If it has already been set to `true`, they just return no errors (or `false` in case of `hasErrors`).

Except for removing the possibility of infinite recursion, this change does not change any method signatures, and keeps the existing behavior identical. All tests in `EntityTest.php` were successful and I added two additional tests to check that infinite recusion does in fact not occur.

If this fix is fine for everyone, I'll also write one for 5.x.
